idiom_name: worker function ranging over the input channel
implementation_notes: There is no endpoint object to write: a function that ranges over the input channel, calls the service and sends the result on the output channel is the service activator, and starting it with go is the consumer. The official pipelines article describes exactly this stage shape - goroutines that receive values from inbound channels, perform their function and send values downstream - and fan-out (competing consumers) comes free by starting several workers on the same channel. Hand-write an endpoint struct only when one endpoint must own per-message policy (retry budget, acknowledgement) or dispatch to different services by message type.
pitfalls: A worker that returns silently, or panics, leaves producers blocked forever on an unbuffered channel; senders need a done channel or context cancellation, as the official pipelines article demonstrates.
Errors have no channel of their own: unless every failure is published to an error or reply channel, the caller waits for a reply that will never arrive - Go's version of a lost message.
Closing a channel is the sender's job; a worker that closes the shared input channel panics the next producer.
